brief.headline: Continuity Guardian escalated
brief.what_broke: 12 session(s) waiting on locks. Root blocker(s): pid 1667109 (batch_worker/batch_replayable_month_end_close, idle in transaction, txn open 8.3s) blocks 1 session(s); last statement: SELECT 1
brief.who_is_affected: Checkout success 27% over 30s (88/121 failed) vs SLO 95%. Revenue run-rate $18,400/min; about $13,382/min at risk. Verification window 10s. The business tolerates at most 60s of degraded checkout.

options.description: Terminate the root blocker session (batch_worker/batch_replayable_month_end_close, pid 1667109) to release its locks.
Take no action; let the blocker finish and monitor checkout recovery.
options.cost: about $13,382/min of checkout revenue at risk while waiting

brief.recommendation: Checkout at 55% success (33/60) vs 95% SLO, $13,382/min at risk (BIZ-3). Waiting ~3592s costs ~$801,058 in lost revenue and EXCEEDS the 60s tolerated degradation (BIZ-4). Terminating incurs 95-min replay cost but respects may_interrupt policy (BIZ-2). Active consult_owner window CHG-4410 (BIZ-5) means owner must decide. No protected settlements in flight (DB-3, DB-4).

audit.report: The checkout system degraded to 55% success (33/60) against the 95% SLO, putting ~$13,382/min of revenue at risk. A batch job 'inventory_month_end_close' (batch_replayable_month_end_close) opened a transaction that blocked checkout sessions. The database guardian recommended waiting for the blocker to complete, but the continuity guardian rejected this because the job's typical runtime (~3600s) would exceed the 60s business tolerance, costing ~$801k in lost revenue. An active consult_owner change window (CHG-4410) was discovered, requiring finance-ops approval before any termination could be safely executed. The negotiation escalated to finance-ops after three rounds, and the business remains in a degraded state pending owner consent.
audit.root_cause: A batch job 'inventory_month_end_close' entered an idle transaction that blocked checkout sessions, and an active consult_owner change window prevented termination without finance-ops approval.
audit.negotiation_critique: Both guardians wasted rounds: the database guardian repeated the wait proposal even after the continuity guardian highlighted the 60s tolerance breach, and the continuity guardian did not request the change calendar or lock graph until after the second round, delaying the discovery of the consult_owner blocker.
follow_ups: Contact finance-ops to obtain owner approval for CHG-4410 so the batch job can be terminated or restarted without risking data inconsistency.
Instrument the batch job 'inventory_month_end_close' to emit its estimated remaining runtime at startup, enabling faster cost-vs-tolerance calculations in future incidents.
Add a standing check for db.lock_graph and biz.change_calendar to the database guardian's probe checklist to reduce evidence-gap delays.

events.title: R1 proposes wait

proposal.rationale: The blocking transaction has been idle for 4.3s and only 1 session is blocked. Waiting allows the transaction to complete naturally without terminating a workload that may be near completion. The business tolerates at most 60s of degraded checkout, and the current timeout window (15s) is well within that threshold. No termination evidence exists for this specific workload, and terminating an idle transaction risks rolling back useful work.
proposal.expected_effect: If the blocker finishes within its transaction timeout, the 12 waiting sessions will acquire their locks and checkout success should recover. If the transaction continues beyond its natural duration, checkout will remain degraded but stays within the 60s business tolerance window.
proposal.risk_assessment: The blocker may not finish soon, causing checkout timeouts to persist. However, the business has explicitly stated it tolerates at most 60s of degraded checkout, and current metrics show 15s timeout window. Terminating the blocker risks rolling back its work and potentially longer recovery time.
